title: Tide and Promise
premise: Eleven years ago, Odile Galloway left Saltmere Bay the night after a devastating fire, taking a scholarship that saved her family's failing bookshop and abandoning Cormac Hale, who never knew why she went. When a storm-damaged mailbag washes up containing a letter she wrote him and never mailed, Odile returns to the town she fled, reopening the bookshop and reopening every wound. As Cormac — now the town's harbormaster and a widowed father — reads the truth of her sacrifice, old loyalty and new resentment war with a love neither has outgrown. But the letter's revelation threatens her career back in the city, and a developer's deadline to buy the bookshop forces her final choice: she stays, sells her stake in the firm that made her, and chooses the tide-worn town and the man who finally sees her whole.
about_author: Sable Underhill is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who now writes love stories from a cottage on the northern coast. Her fiction is known for salt-weathered settings and heroines who mistake sacrifice for strength.

chapters.title: The Unmailed Year
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In her city office, Odile receives a water-stained parcel: her own letter from eleven years ago, returned undelivered. She reads the words she wrote Cormac the night before she left Saltmere Bay. Emotional beat: dread and vertigo as the past she sealed away cracks open.

chapters.title: Saltmere, Again
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She drives back to the bay, finding her aunt's bookshop shuttered and the town half-gentrified. She signs papers to reopen it, telling herself it's only for the summer. Emotional beat: homesickness tangled with guilt; she is a stranger in her own history.

chapters.title: Harbormaster
chapters.summary: Cormac's POV. Cormac sees Odile's name on the shop lease and feels eleven years of anger ignite. His daughter Nell senses his mood shift. Emotional beat: wounded pride masking grief he never processed after his wife's death.

chapters.title: First Words
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Their first encounter in the bookshop is barbed and electric; Cormac accuses, Odile deflects, neither mentions the letter. Nell wanders in and takes an instant liking to Odile. Emotional beat: the pull beneath the hostility, undeniable and unwelcome.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Restocking the shop, Odile finds marginalia in her late aunt's hand — notes about the fire, hinting it wasn't an accident. Emotional beat: unease; the letter may be only the first secret surfacing.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Cormac's POV. Cormac learns a development consortium wants the harborfront — including the bookshop — and that Odile's old firm is brokering the deal. Emotional beat: protective fury; he assumes Odile has come to sell them out.

chapters.title: Nell's Borrowed Book
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell sneaks into the shop, borrows a novel, and leaves a note. Odile, recognizing her younger self in the girl, begins a quiet correspondence of margin notes. Emotional beat: tenderness blooming where Odile least expects it.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A gale traps Odile and Cormac in the shop overnight repairing storm shutters. Forced proximity cracks the silence; they argue about the fire, the leaving, the letter — but she still can't confess. Emotional beat: longing at war with self-protection.

chapters.title: What the Margins Say
chapters.summary: Cormac's POV. Cormac discovers Nell's margin-notes with Odile and confronts her — but the sight of his daughter laughing undoes him. He asks, for the first time, why she really left. Emotional beat: the armor slipping; a question he's carried eleven years finally spoken.

chapters.title: Half the Truth
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile tells Cormac about the scholarship and her family's debts but omits that her firm engineered the fire's insurance denial — the truth in her aunt's notes. Emotional beat: shame compounding; loyalty to her career versus loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: The Consortium Calls
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Her city mentor arrives with a lucrative offer: lead the harborfront project and make partner. The deadline is thirty days. Emotional beat: the trap closing — the career that saved her now demanding she betray the town.

chapters.title: Kiss in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Cormac's POV. After a town meeting where Cormac publicly defends the bookshop, he and Odile give in to eleven years of wanting. Emotional beat: joy and terror in equal measure; the past tense becoming present.

chapters.title: Nell's Wish
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell, hopeful and perceptive, tells Odile she wishes she'd stay forever — and mentions her father still keeps a box of Odile's old letters. Emotional beat: the weight of being someone's hope; stakes made personal.

chapters.title: The Fire, Reconsidered
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile digs into her aunt's notes and the insurance records, confirming her firm falsified the fire report to force the sale — the sale that funded her scholarship. Emotional beat: horror; her entire life was built on a lie she didn't know she inherited.

chapters.title: Confession and Cost
chapters.summary: Cormac's POV. Odile tells Cormac everything. His loyalty to the town wars with his love for her; he asks for time. Emotional beat: heartbreak with an open door — truth offered too late to be painless.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The consortium forces the issue: sign the harborfront deal or lose her partnership. Her mentor gives her an ultimatum and a plane ticket. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal; everything she built weighed against everything she loves.

chapters.title: The Empty Shop
chapters.summary: Cormac's POV. Cormac finds the shop closed, Odile's lease papers and a resignation draft left behind. He believes she's gone back to the city and the deal. Emotional beat: despair hardening into resolve to fight the developers alone.

chapters.title: What Cormac Never Read
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell gives her father the box — and the returned letter Odile left inside it, addressed to him. He finally reads the words written eleven years ago. Emotional beat: devastation and clarity; seeing her whole at last.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the town hall vote on the harborfront sale, Odile returns mid-session and testifies against her own firm, exposing the falsified fire report. Emotional beat: the climax of truth — burning her career to save the town and herself.

chapters.title: Running Out of Tide
chapters.summary: Cormac's POV. With the deal dead and Odile's future in ruins, Cormac searches for her at the harbor as the tide turns. He finds her at the old pier where they parted. Emotional beat: the grand gesture inverted — he offers her nothing but the truth that he sees her, and asks her to stay.

chapters.title: Tide and Promise
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile chooses Saltmere: the shop reopens under both their names, her testimony sparks an investigation, and she begins rebuilding on honest ground. Emotional beat: resolution — love chosen not despite the past, but with it fully known.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Margins, One Year Later
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. A year on, Nell writes in the shop's guestbook; Odile and Cormac are planning a small wedding on the pier. The returned letter is framed above the till. Emotional beat: quiet fullness — memory honored, loyalty and truth finally on the same side.
